name: Aboriginal didgeridoo solo songlines (extended)
lineage: Aboriginal Australian songlines tradition embedding the didgeridoo (Yolngu yiḏaki) as both instrument and oral-historical-mnemonic system mapping landscape across Arnhem Land (Northern Territory) and the broader Top End. The yiḏaki is a hollowed eucalyptus-trunk natural-trumpet played with constant-airflow circular-breathing technique. Performance contexts span the manikay public ceremonial-song tradition (which is sung-vocal with clapsticks plus yiḏaki accompaniment) and the more specialized initiation-ceremony repertoire restricted to initiated men. Each manikay cycle maps a specific songline-route across the country, encoding geographic and ancestral knowledge. Distinguished from the broader generic didgeridoo-solo by manikay's ceremonial-functional context and Yolngu-specific yiḏaki performance lineage.
